description:
We are a team of enthusiastic CSE students passionate about space, science, technology and innovation. We aim to explore real-world challenges using NASA data and develop creative, practical solutions. We welcome curious minds who enjoy learning, collaborating and thinking outside the box.

We are looking for teammates with interests in Python, web development, data analysis, UI/UX design, research and creative problem-solving. Beginners with enthusiasm and a willingness to learn are welcome!
summary:
The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based space exploration simulator designed to introduce elementary students to aerospace engineering, space science, and robotics through hands-on learning.

We developed a six-mission training platform that follows a Plan → Execute → Evaluate approach. Students can assemble and launch rockets, manage space station life-support systems, establish lunar bases, program Mars rovers, design Earth-observation satellites, and simulate asteroid deflection. The platform combines realistic physics calculations, interactive simulations, coding activities, and post-mission assessments to make complex scientific concepts accessible and engaging.

It addresses the challenge of making STEM education more practical, immersive, and inclusive by transforming theoretical concepts into interactive space missions. With COPPA-compliant zero-PII student accounts, educator dashboards, accessibility features, and NGSS-aligned learning outcomes, the platform provides a safe and inclusive learning environment.

Our goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts by making space exploration an engaging educational experience.
details:
Project Details

The Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer is an interactive, browser-based STEM learning platform designed for children aged 5–11. It transforms space science and aerospace engineering into an engaging, hands-on learning experience through six simulated space missions.

How It Works:

The platform follows a Plan → Execute → Evaluate learning cycle. Students begin by assembling rockets, selecting engines, fuel tanks, and payloads while observing real-time physics calculations such as mass, thrust, Delta-V, and thrust-to-weight ratio. They then execute simulated rocket launches featuring countdowns, engine effects, atmospheric transitions, and orbital velocity tracking.

Beyond rocket launches, students can manage space station life-support systems, design lunar bases, program Mars rovers using drag-and-drop commands, configure Earth-observation satellites, and simulate asteroid deflection. Each mission includes learning assessments, progress tracking, and achievement badges.

Technology and Tools Used:

  • Frontend: React 18, TypeScript, Vite and Tailwind CSS.
  • Backend: Node.js with a custom REST API.
  • Database: JSON-based data storage.
  • Physics: Newton's laws of motion, Tsiolkovsky's Delta-V equation, and atmospheric drag simulation.
  • Audio: Web Audio API and Web Speech API.
  • Security: COPPA validation middleware, input sanitization, and zero-PII data handling.
  • Testing: Node.js native test runner.

The application is developed as a browser-based software solution and does not require dedicated external hardware.

Benefits and Intended Impact:

The project makes complex scientific concepts easier to understand through interactive experimentation rather than traditional textbook learning. It encourages critical thinking, problem-solving, computational thinking, creativity, and engineering skills. Educators can monitor classroom progress, track mission completion, and evaluate student understanding through a dedicated command center.

Creativity and Innovation:

The project's uniqueness lies in combining six different areas of space exploration into one educational platform. Instead of simply learning about rockets, planets, and satellites, children actively participate in simulated missions and experience the consequences of their engineering decisions.

Factors Considered:

Our team considered age-appropriate learning, scientific accuracy, accessibility, child safety, data privacy, usability, and educational relevance. Features such as adjustable text sizes, high-contrast mode, colorblind-friendly patterns, keyboard navigation, and voice narration make the platform more inclusive. COPPA-compliant zero-PII architecture helps create a safer digital learning environment.

Ultimately, our vision is to make aerospace education accessible, interactive, and inspiring, encouraging young learners to explore STEM and become tomorrow's scientists, engineers, and astronauts.
